assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalysed C-N cross-coupling turned aryl amine formation from a niche, forcing process into a routine, general bond construction used across medicinal and process chemistry; few methods have changed how chemists build bonds more widely. Conceptually clear (oxidative addition, amine binding, reductive elimination) and pervasive in the literature.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the ligand-controlled, general catalytic systems that made the reaction broadly useful. Kosugi (and Migita) reported earlier tin-amide couplings, a precursor with limited scope; I would not give him a place in a prize of at most three, though the precursor question needs to be acknowledged.
assessment.maturity: Mature: three decades of adoption, industrial use at scale and extensive mechanistic confirmation. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Weight of Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work versus the later general catalytic systems is a judgement call; I have not verified the exact priority dates.
Whether the committee views cross-coupling as already honoured by the 2010 prize and so closed to further related recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Directed and ligand-accelerated C-H functionalization lets chemists form C-C and C-heteroatom bonds at otherwise unreactive positions, shortening syntheses and rewriting retrosynthetic logic. Strongly aligned with efficiency in synthesis, and visibly used in late-stage functionalization and total synthesis.
assessment.attribution: Yu (ligand design, remote and enantioselective C-H activation), Sanford (Pd(II)/Pd(IV) catalysis and oxidant-based functionalization) and Daugulis (aminoquinoline directing groups) each made distinct, decisive contributions. Hartwig's borylation work is also credited here but overlaps another candidate, and Milton Smith's borylation role is real but narrower; choosing three is a judgement among several good claims.
assessment.maturity: Largely mature in scope but still developing in selectivity and generality; industrial use is growing. Somewhat earlier in its arc than C-N coupling, though recognition is plausible now.
uncertainties: A cleaner prize might be organised around a narrower concept (directing-group-based Pd C-H activation), and the field is crowded with credit claimants.
Practical limits (stoichiometric oxidants, directing-group removal, substrate scope) remain; I cannot independently verify current industrial adoption.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation made chemically precise assembly of proteins from unprotected peptide segments routine, with a clean chemoselective bond-forming concept (thioester exchange, S-to-N acyl shift). It is real molecule-making: total chemical synthesis of proteins, semisynthesis and many biological applications.
assessment.attribution: Kent and Dawson developed and published native chemical ligation in 1994; Muir contributed expressed protein ligation, which extended the concept to semisynthesis. Danishefsky, Brik and Liu made important extensions (desulfurisation, glycoprotein and ubiquitin synthesis) but are less central to the origin.
assessment.maturity: The method is over 30 years old, widely used and confirmed in many laboratories; recognition is timely. Impact on biology is demonstrated, though routine large-scale use is still largely academic or in peptide therapeutics.
uncertainties: Ordering of credit between Kent, Dawson and Muir, and whether to credit Danishefsky for the broader synthetic programme.
The relative scientific weight of protein synthesis versus recombinant expression, which has become dominant for many targets.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bergman's demonstration of intermolecular oxidative addition of unactivated alkane C-H bonds to iridium complexes (early 1980s) proved a long-doubted reaction was possible and founded the field of C-H activation. Conceptually fundamental, with a clear lasting influence on synthetic and catalysis thinking.
assessment.attribution: A single-person credit is clear, though Graham (Janowicz and Bergman at Berkeley, Graham at Rochester) published near-simultaneously; the supplied credit lists only Bergman, so priority and co-credit with Graham and later Jones, Periana and Goldman should be considered.
assessment.maturity: Fundamental result is well confirmed and widely taught; practical catalysis from alkane activation remains limited, so the case rests on concept rather than adoption. Timing is mature, perhaps late.
uncertainties: Impact is conceptual rather than directly practical; the committee may weigh that against methods used daily.
I am uncertain of the exact attribution detail regarding Graham's parallel work, and Bergman may be proposed alone only if that is judged fair.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis gave synthetic chemists mild single-electron-transfer reactivity for radical generation, now ubiquitous in medicinal and academic synthesis and used in many new bond constructions, including dual catalysis with transition metals.
assessment.attribution: Yoon, Stephenson and MacMillan reported the 2008-2009 foundational synthetic applications; Nicewicz, Fukuzumi, König and Melchiorre made further important contributions, and earlier inorganic photochemistry (Kellogg, Cano-Yelo and Deronzier, and others) sits in the background. MacMillan has already received a Nobel Prize (organocatalysis, 2021, as I recall), which may reduce the committee's appetite and complicates a three-person configuration.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted and rapidly maturing; industrial flow and scale-up uses are emerging. Possibly slightly early for a discovery with continuing evolution, but impact is evident.
uncertainties: Prior laureate status of MacMillan and the many comparable claimants make a fair configuration difficult.
Distinction between new concept and re-application of known photochemistry is arguable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Frustrated Lewis pairs showed that sterically hindered Lewis acid-base pairs can heterolytically activate H2 and other small molecules without a transition metal, opening metal-free hydrogenation and a new view of main-group reactivity. Chemically novel and conceptually simple.
assessment.attribution: Stephan's 2006 metal-free reversible H2 activation and Erker's related work on intramolecular and alkene-based FLPs are the central contributions; the two-person configuration is reasonably clean, though Tamm, Piers and others contributed.
assessment.maturity: About 20 years old, replicated broadly, but practical impact (catalytic hydrogenation at scale) has been modest so far; maturity is moderate.
uncertainties: Practical adoption lags behind the conceptual excitement.
Whether the committee regards it as a major shift or a niche in main-group chemistry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion, using orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs to site-specifically incorporate non-canonical amino acids, gave chemists a way to place designed chemistry in proteins in living cells. It is widely used and has a clear conceptual core, though I would ask what is chemically new beyond the biological machinery.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang established the first orthogonal pairs in E. coli and eukaryotes; Chin extended the work to multicellular organisms and to quadruplet codons and genomically recoded organisms. Mehl and Yokoyama contributed important systems; I choose the three with the clearest broad programmes.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed, widely used in labs, and increasingly in biologic drug development; timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Border with biology: the committee may see it as molecular biology rather than chemistry.
Allocation of credit among five names is contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The isolation of stable carbenes, first the crystalline N-heterocyclic carbene and the earlier stable phosphinocarbenes, changed bonding concepts and gave a ligand class that now underpins ruthenium metathesis, Pd cross-coupling and organocatalysis. Chemical novelty is high and downstream use in synthesis is very large.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand's 1988 phosphino(silyl)carbene and Arduengo's 1991 imidazol-2-ylidene are the key isolations; Nolan, Rovis and Bode are credited for applying carbenes in catalysis and organocatalysis. Choosing Arduengo and Bertrand reflects the discovery rather than the applications.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, with three decades of use; recognition is timely though some of the impact has been rewarded indirectly through metathesis.
uncertainties: Overlap with the metathesis prize of 2005 may weaken the case.
Whether ligand development or the isolation itself is the decisive achievement.
